boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Opequon (Third Winchester) record (September 19, 1864) in Sheridan's Valley Campaign [August-October 1864]. Early's September 17-18 move to Martinsburg and the September 20 pursuit are context. Campaign-wide marches, destruction, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen and live force fields read 54,440 total (US 39,240; CS 15,200); the source basis is not given. Early says Sheridan's infantry was nearly if not quite three times his own and his cavalry much superior, and on September 25 put the odds at three or four to one. Pond's appendix computes Early's infantry plus Fitz Lee at 17,195 without Kershaw (from a September 10 return) and gives Sheridan's September 10 field return as 45,509 corrected, excluding about 2,500 of Averell's cavalry. Pond says Grover's division had an effective strength of 6,797 just before the battle.
claims.rationale: Early's ratios are interested estimates; the returns are dated nine days before and do not measure the force engaged. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty fields read 8,630 total (US 5,020; CS 3,610). Early gives his infantry and artillery loss as 226 killed (read 22G in OCR), 1,567 wounded and 1,818 missing, total 3,611, with no full cavalry report; Pond reproduces an unsigned memorandum giving 199 killed and 1,508 wounded, total 1,707. Pond puts the Union loss at 4,900 to 5,000 and Early's at 3,900 to 4,000, nearly 2,000 of them prisoners. Early reports hearsay of 5,800 Union wounded in Winchester hospitals.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Early's September 1-October 1 cavalry figure (348 killed and wounded) spans several actions and is not added.

open_questions: Sheridan's 1866 report passage on the battle (read, not selected), his September 19 dispatch, Wright's, Emory's, Crook's, Torbert's and the division reports, the compiled Union returns (Nos. 3-4) and Hotchkiss's journal remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. George E. Pond's The Shenandoah Valley in 1864 (Scribner, 1883) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, from the official documents at the War Records Office and field despatches; it quotes Sheridan's, Torbert's, Wright's and Early's reports and despatches and is not independent of them. Early's reports and dispatches of September 23-October 21, 1864 to Lee are one family of interested Confederate accounts; it is the same author family as his July 14 report selected for Early's Raid. Official Records Series I, Volume XLIII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
